assumptions: 3 of 874 stations have no usable RX or TX frequency and were skipped, so they are not protected here.

RX and TX frequencies are both protected, because Traficom said "every TX is received in Finland" (Discord, 2026-11-07): around a broadcast transmitter, or at the far end of a fixed link. matched_on gives the side each station matched; "both" means its RX and TX bands are the same.
A station's band is its frequency +/- half its channel bandwidth, or half its transmission bandwidth where the channel bandwidth is blank. Where the two differ, the channel bandwidth is used.
The station data is synthetic, per Traficom.

Each station's result comes from the pfd rule's calculation at its coordinates, over the part of the band a limit mask covers. A part with no mask, or a mask that needs an input the filing lacks, counts as no calculation, and a slight edge overlap counts.

Beam coverage is not checked: s_beam gives no boresight in this data, and Traficom said beams "are not relevant" and "the worst case scenario should always be assumed" (Discord, 2026-11-07), so maximum notified gain is applied towards every station.
Antenna direction is not checked: the satellite's is not in the data, and the sheet gives a station direction but few gains, and the receive gain to assume is unanswered (ticket 02 question 14).

Severity follows the strongest evidence at any station: a calculated exceedance is high; a value within 3 dB, an upper bound near or above the limit, or no calculation is medium; a calculated value below, or a satellite below every station's horizon, is low. This severity is the project's choice, not Traficom's.

title: CSN-SSO (CHN) transmits on a band of 515 protected station(s): BT 56, Earth station (RX) 1, FX 320, MUUT 8, MVV 61, no class 69; pfd exceeds the limit at 15 listed stations under worst-case assumptions

assumptions: 3 of 874 stations have no usable RX or TX frequency and were skipped, so they are not protected here.

RX and TX frequencies are both protected, because Traficom said "every TX is received in Finland" (Discord, 2026-11-07): around a broadcast transmitter, or at the far end of a fixed link. matched_on gives the side each station matched; "both" means its RX and TX bands are the same.
A station's band is its frequency +/- half its channel bandwidth, or half its transmission bandwidth where the channel bandwidth is blank. Where the two differ, the channel bandwidth is used.
The station data is synthetic, per Traficom.

Each station's result comes from the pfd rule's calculation at its coordinates, over the part of the band a limit mask covers. A part with no mask, or a mask that needs an input the filing lacks, counts as no calculation, and a slight edge overlap counts.

Beam coverage is not checked: s_beam gives no boresight in this data, and Traficom said beams "are not relevant" and "the worst case scenario should always be assumed" (Discord, 2026-11-07), so maximum notified gain is applied towards every station.
Antenna direction is not checked: the satellite's is not in the data, and the sheet gives a station direction but few gains, and the receive gain to assume is unanswered (ticket 02 question 14).

Severity follows the strongest evidence at any station: a calculated exceedance is high; a value within 3 dB, an upper bound near or above the limit, or no calculation is medium; a calculated value below, or a satellite below every station's horizon, is low. This severity is the project's choice, not Traficom's.

title: CHINASAT-H-60.5E (CHN) transmits on a band of 374 protected station(s): Earth station (RX) 1, FX 320, MUUT 8, MVV 11, no class 34; pfd exceeds the limit at 29 listed stations under worst-case assumptions

assumptions: 3 of 874 stations have no usable RX or TX frequency and were skipped, so they are not protected here.

RX and TX frequencies are both protected, because Traficom said "every TX is received in Finland" (Discord, 2026-11-07): around a broadcast transmitter, or at the far end of a fixed link. matched_on gives the side each station matched; "both" means its RX and TX bands are the same.
A station's band is its frequency +/- half its channel bandwidth, or half its transmission bandwidth where the channel bandwidth is blank. Where the two differ, the channel bandwidth is used.
The station data is synthetic, per Traficom.

Each station's result comes from the pfd rule's calculation at its coordinates, over the part of the band a limit mask covers. A part with no mask, or a mask that needs an input the filing lacks, counts as no calculation, and a slight edge overlap counts.

Beam coverage is not checked: s_beam gives no boresight in this data, and Traficom said beams "are not relevant" and "the worst case scenario should always be assumed" (Discord, 2026-11-07), so maximum notified gain is applied towards every station.
Antenna direction is not checked: the satellite's is not in the data, and the sheet gives a station direction but few gains, and the receive gain to assume is unanswered (ticket 02 question 14).

Severity follows the strongest evidence at any station: a calculated exceedance is high; a value within 3 dB, an upper bound near or above the limit, or no calculation is medium; a calculated value below, or a satellite below every station's horizon, is low. This severity is the project's choice, not Traficom's.

title: CHINASAT-G-33.5E (CHN) transmits on a band of 374 protected station(s): Earth station (RX) 1, FX 320, MUUT 8, MVV 11, no class 34; pfd exceeds the limit at 20 listed stations under worst-case assumptions

assumptions: Results are possible concerns for expert review; they do not establish compliance.
Records with missing inputs are counted for expert review. Not visible from Finland is a computed result, counted separately.
Mask rows are chosen by band and, for non-GSO, orbit shape, not by the filing's service.

Stations are those in Traficom's list whose RX or TX band overlaps the part of an assignment the mask covers. A GSO value at a station is calculated at its coordinates. A non-GSO value at a station is a sample from the same one-day flight, not a bound; the upper bound has no location, so it applies to the filing and is never given as a station value.
A station's coordinates are not where its TX band is received, so a margin at the site for a TX match is not a margin at the receiver (field_location says so).
The envelope pairs each arrival angle with the shortest distance the orbit can have at that angle, for any node, phase, epoch or argument of perigee, at altitudes from notified perigee to apogee.
Latitude reach comes from inclination and the southernmost Finnish point; relative longitude is unconstrained.
Where orbit_lnk names the orbit rows a beam flies on, only those rows are used. This reading of orbit_lnk is not confirmed against the primary Space Preface.
The envelope is sampled every 0.02 degrees of arrival angle, including every mask breakpoint.
The envelope does not cover station-keeping excursions beyond the notified altitudes, or more than one satellite adding up at a point. It may describe states the satellite never occupies.
Propagation is two-body with no J2, over one day in one-minute steps, for one satellite per distinct orbit shape, so it can miss the worst case and is not an upper bound.

No epoch is notified: at minute 0 the node lies at the notified long_asc (or right_asc if that is absent) as an Earth-fixed longitude, and the satellite is phase_ang past the node. These field meanings are not confirmed against the primary Space Preface.
Free-space propagation (RR No. 21.16).
Angle of arrival is geometric elevation on a spherical Earth, with no refraction.
Maximum notified gain applies towards every point at every moment. With boresight gain this over-estimates pfd off-axis.
pwr_ds_max is treated as dBW/Hz per a secondary schema note; primary Space Preface confirmation is unavailable.

Power in the reference bandwidth is pwr_ds_max plus 10 log10(reference bandwidth), capped by the row's pep_max, treated as dBW; the emission row used is the one with the most power after that cap. A row without pep_max is not capped.

title: STARERA-3 (CHN) NGSO Article 21 limit exceeds in a one-day propagation under worst-case assumptions; 8 listed stations in band

assumptions: Results are possible concerns for expert review; they do not establish compliance.

A non-GSO value at a station is a sample from the same one-day flight, not a bound; the upper bound has no location, so it applies to the filing and is never given as a station value.
A station's coordinates are not where its TX band is received, so a margin at the site for a TX match is not a margin at the receiver (field_location says so).

Power in the reference bandwidth is pwr_ds_max plus 10 log10(reference bandwidth), capped by the row's pep_max, treated as dBW; the emission row used is the one with the most power after that cap. A row without pep_max is not capped.
Maximum gain and power density are used for the whole assignment.

title: CHINASAT-G-33.5E (CHN) GSO Appendix 5 coordination trigger exceeds under worst-case assumptions; 1 listed station in band, exceeds at 1

assumptions: Results are possible concerns for expert review; they do not establish compliance.
Records with missing inputs are counted for expert review. Not visible from Finland is a computed result, counted separately.
Mask rows are chosen by band and, for non-GSO, orbit shape, not by the filing's service.

Stations are those in Traficom's list whose RX or TX band overlaps the part of an assignment the mask covers. A GSO value at a station is calculated at its coordinates. A non-GSO value at a station is a sample from the same one-day flight, not a bound; the upper bound has no location, so it applies to the filing and is never given as a station value.
A station's coordinates are not where its TX band is received, so a margin at the site for a TX match is not a margin at the receiver (field_location says so).
The envelope pairs each arrival angle with the shortest distance the orbit can have at that angle, for any node, phase, epoch or argument of perigee, at altitudes from notified perigee to apogee.
Latitude reach comes from inclination and the southernmost Finnish point; relative longitude is unconstrained.
Where orbit_lnk names the orbit rows a beam flies on, only those rows are used. This reading of orbit_lnk is not confirmed against the primary Space Preface.
The envelope is sampled every 0.02 degrees of arrival angle, including every mask breakpoint.
The envelope does not cover station-keeping excursions beyond the notified altitudes, or more than one satellite adding up at a point. It may describe states the satellite never occupies.
Propagation is two-body with no J2, over one day in one-minute steps, for one satellite per distinct orbit shape, so it can miss the worst case and is not an upper bound.

No epoch is notified: at minute 0 the node lies at the notified long_asc (or right_asc if that is absent) as an Earth-fixed longitude, and the satellite is phase_ang past the node. These field meanings are not confirmed against the primary Space Preface.
Free-space propagation (RR No. 21.16).
Angle of arrival is geometric elevation on a spherical Earth, with no refraction.
Maximum notified gain applies towards every point at every moment. With boresight gain this over-estimates pfd off-axis.
pwr_ds_max is treated as dBW/Hz per a secondary schema note; primary Space Preface confirmation is unavailable.

Power in the reference bandwidth is pwr_ds_max plus 10 log10(reference bandwidth), capped by the row's pep_max, treated as dBW; the emission row used is the one with the most power after that cap. A row without pep_max is not capped.

Where orbit_lnk names the orbit rows a beam flies on, only those rows are used. This reading of orbit_lnk is not confirmed against the primary Space Preface.
The envelope is sampled every 0.02 degrees of arrival angle, including every mask breakpoint.
The envelope does not cover station-keeping excursions beyond the notified altitudes, or more than one satellite adding up at a point. It may describe states the satellite never occupies.
Propagation is two-body with no J2, over one day in one-minute steps, for one satellite per distinct orbit shape, so it can miss the worst case and is not an upper bound.

No epoch is notified: at minute 0 the node lies at the notified long_asc (or right_asc if that is absent) as an Earth-fixed longitude, and the satellite is phase_ang past the node. These field meanings are not confirmed against the primary Space Preface.
Free-space propagation (RR No. 21.16).
Angle of arrival is geometric elevation on a spherical Earth, with no refraction.
Maximum notified gain applies towards every point at every moment. With boresight gain this over-estimates pfd off-axis.
pwr_ds_max is treated as dBW/Hz per a secondary schema note; primary Space Preface confirmation is unavailable.

Power in the reference bandwidth is pwr_ds_max plus 10 log10(reference bandwidth), capped by the row's pep_max, treated as dBW; the emission row used is the one with the most power after that cap. A row without pep_max is not capped.

Where orbit_lnk names the orbit rows a beam flies on, only those rows are used. This reading of orbit_lnk is not confirmed against the primary Space Preface.
The envelope is sampled every 0.02 degrees of arrival angle, including every mask breakpoint.
The envelope does not cover station-keeping excursions beyond the notified altitudes, or more than one satellite adding up at a point. It may describe states the satellite never occupies.
Propagation is two-body with no J2, over one day in one-minute steps, for one satellite per distinct orbit shape, so it can miss the worst case and is not an upper bound.

No epoch is notified: at minute 0 the node lies at the notified long_asc (or right_asc if that is absent) as an Earth-fixed longitude, and the satellite is phase_ang past the node. These field meanings are not confirmed against the primary Space Preface.
Free-space propagation (RR No. 21.16).
Angle of arrival is geometric elevation on a spherical Earth, with no refraction.
Maximum notified gain applies towards every point at every moment. With boresight gain this over-estimates pfd off-axis.
pwr_ds_max is treated as dBW/Hz per a secondary schema note; primary Space Preface confirmation is unavailable.

Power in the reference bandwidth is pwr_ds_max plus 10 log10(reference bandwidth), capped by the row's pep_max, treated as dBW; the emission row used is the one with the most power after that cap. A row without pep_max is not capped.

Where orbit_lnk names the orbit rows a beam flies on, only those rows are used. This reading of orbit_lnk is not confirmed against the primary Space Preface.
The envelope is sampled every 0.02 degrees of arrival angle, including every mask breakpoint.
The envelope does not cover station-keeping excursions beyond the notified altitudes, or more than one satellite adding up at a point. It may describe states the satellite never occupies.
Propagation is two-body with no J2, over one day in one-minute steps, for one satellite per distinct orbit shape, so it can miss the worst case and is not an upper bound.

No epoch is notified: at minute 0 the node lies at the notified long_asc (or right_asc if that is absent) as an Earth-fixed longitude, and the satellite is phase_ang past the node. These field meanings are not confirmed against the primary Space Preface.
Free-space propagation (RR No. 21.16).
Angle of arrival is geometric elevation on a spherical Earth, with no refraction.
Maximum notified gain applies towards every point at every moment. With boresight gain this over-estimates pfd off-axis.
pwr_ds_max is treated as dBW/Hz per a secondary schema note; primary Space Preface confirmation is unavailable.

Power in the reference bandwidth is pwr_ds_max plus 10 log10(reference bandwidth), capped by the row's pep_max, treated as dBW; the emission row used is the one with the most power after that cap. A row without pep_max is not capped.

Where orbit_lnk names the orbit rows a beam flies on, only those rows are used. This reading of orbit_lnk is not confirmed against the primary Space Preface.
The envelope is sampled every 0.02 degrees of arrival angle, including every mask breakpoint.
The envelope does not cover station-keeping excursions beyond the notified altitudes, or more than one satellite adding up at a point. It may describe states the satellite never occupies.
Propagation is two-body with no J2, over one day in one-minute steps, for one satellite per distinct orbit shape, so it can miss the worst case and is not an upper bound.

No epoch is notified: at minute 0 the node lies at the notified long_asc (or right_asc if that is absent) as an Earth-fixed longitude, and the satellite is phase_ang past the node. These field meanings are not confirmed against the primary Space Preface.
Free-space propagation (RR No. 21.16).
Angle of arrival is geometric elevation on a spherical Earth, with no refraction.
Maximum notified gain applies towards every point at every moment. With boresight gain this over-estimates pfd off-axis.
pwr_ds_max is treated as dBW/Hz per a secondary schema note; primary Space Preface confirmation is unavailable.

Power in the reference bandwidth is pwr_ds_max plus 10 log10(reference bandwidth), capped by the row's pep_max, treated as dBW; the emission row used is the one with the most power after that cap. A row without pep_max is not capped.

Where orbit_lnk names the orbit rows a beam flies on, only those rows are used. This reading of orbit_lnk is not confirmed against the primary Space Preface.
The envelope is sampled every 0.02 degrees of arrival angle, including every mask breakpoint.
The envelope does not cover station-keeping excursions beyond the notified altitudes, or more than one satellite adding up at a point. It may describe states the satellite never occupies.
Propagation is two-body with no J2, over one day in one-minute steps, for one satellite per distinct orbit shape, so it can miss the worst case and is not an upper bound.

No epoch is notified: at minute 0 the node lies at the notified long_asc (or right_asc if that is absent) as an Earth-fixed longitude, and the satellite is phase_ang past the node. These field meanings are not confirmed against the primary Space Preface.
Free-space propagation (RR No. 21.16).
Angle of arrival is geometric elevation on a spherical Earth, with no refraction.
Maximum notified gain applies towards every point at every moment. With boresight gain this over-estimates pfd off-axis.
pwr_ds_max is treated as dBW/Hz per a secondary schema note; primary Space Preface confirmation is unavailable.

Power in the reference bandwidth is pwr_ds_max plus 10 log10(reference bandwidth), capped by the row's pep_max, treated as dBW; the emission row used is the one with the most power after that cap. A row without pep_max is not capped.

Where orbit_lnk names the orbit rows a beam flies on, only those rows are used. This reading of orbit_lnk is not confirmed against the primary Space Preface.
The envelope is sampled every 0.02 degrees of arrival angle, including every mask breakpoint.
The envelope does not cover station-keeping excursions beyond the notified altitudes, or more than one satellite adding up at a point. It may describe states the satellite never occupies.
Propagation is two-body with no J2, over one day in one-minute steps, for one satellite per distinct orbit shape, so it can miss the worst case and is not an upper bound.

No epoch is notified: at minute 0 the node lies at the notified long_asc (or right_asc if that is absent) as an Earth-fixed longitude, and the satellite is phase_ang past the node. These field meanings are not confirmed against the primary Space Preface.
Free-space propagation (RR No. 21.16).
Angle of arrival is geometric elevation on a spherical Earth, with no refraction.
Maximum notified gain applies towards every point at every moment. With boresight gain this over-estimates pfd off-axis.
pwr_ds_max is treated as dBW/Hz per a secondary schema note; primary Space Preface confirmation is unavailable.

Power in the reference bandwidth is pwr_ds_max plus 10 log10(reference bandwidth), capped by the row's pep_max, treated as dBW; the emission row used is the one with the most power after that cap. A row without pep_max is not capped.

Where orbit_lnk names the orbit rows a beam flies on, only those rows are used. This reading of orbit_lnk is not confirmed against the primary Space Preface.
The envelope is sampled every 0.02 degrees of arrival angle, including every mask breakpoint.
The envelope does not cover station-keeping excursions beyond the notified altitudes, or more than one satellite adding up at a point. It may describe states the satellite never occupies.
Propagation is two-body with no J2, over one day in one-minute steps, for one satellite per distinct orbit shape, so it can miss the worst case and is not an upper bound.

No epoch is notified: at minute 0 the node lies at the notified long_asc (or right_asc if that is absent) as an Earth-fixed longitude, and the satellite is phase_ang past the node. These field meanings are not confirmed against the primary Space Preface.
Free-space propagation (RR No. 21.16).
Angle of arrival is geometric elevation on a spherical Earth, with no refraction.
Maximum notified gain applies towards every point at every moment. With boresight gain this over-estimates pfd off-axis.
pwr_ds_max is treated as dBW/Hz per a secondary schema note; primary Space Preface confirmation is unavailable.

Power in the reference bandwidth is pwr_ds_max plus 10 log10(reference bandwidth), capped by the row's pep_max, treated as dBW; the emission row used is the one with the most power after that cap. A row without pep_max is not capped.

assumptions: Free-space propagation (RR No. 21.16).
Angle of arrival is geometric elevation on a spherical Earth, with no refraction.
The given gain applies towards every point. With boresight gain this over-estimates pfd off-axis.
pwr_ds_max is treated as dBW/Hz per a secondary schema note; primary Space Preface confirmation is unavailable.

Power in the reference bandwidth is pwr_ds_max plus 10 log10(reference bandwidth), capped by the row's pep_max, treated as dBW; the emission row used is the one with the most power after that cap. A row without pep_max is not capped.
Maximum gain and power density are used for the whole assignment.

assumptions: Free-space propagation (RR No. 21.16).
Angle of arrival is geometric elevation on a spherical Earth, with no refraction.
The given gain applies towards every point. With boresight gain this over-estimates pfd off-axis.
pwr_ds_max is treated as dBW/Hz per a secondary schema note; primary Space Preface confirmation is unavailable.

Power in the reference bandwidth is pwr_ds_max plus 10 log10(reference bandwidth), capped by the row's pep_max, treated as dBW; the emission row used is the one with the most power after that cap. A row without pep_max is not capped.
Maximum gain and power density are used for the whole assignment.

pwr_ds_max is treated as dBW/Hz per a secondary schema note; primary Space Preface confirmation is unavailable.

Power in the reference bandwidth is pwr_ds_max plus 10 log10(reference bandwidth), capped by the row's pep_max, treated as dBW; the emission row used is the one with the most power after that cap. A row without pep_max is not capped.
Maximum gain and power density are used for the whole assignment.

title: INSAT-COM(71E) (IND) GSO Article 21 limit exceeds under worst-case assumptions; 28 listed stations in band, exceeds at 24

assumptions: Results are possible concerns for expert review; they do not establish compliance.
Records with missing inputs are counted for expert review. Not visible from Finland is a computed result, counted separately.
Mask rows are chosen by band and, for non-GSO, orbit shape, not by the filing's service.

Stations are those in Traficom's list whose RX or TX band overlaps the part of an assignment the mask covers. A GSO value at a station is calculated at its coordinates. A non-GSO value at a station is a sample from the same one-day flight, not a bound; the upper bound has no location, so it applies to the filing and is never given as a station value.
A station's coordinates are not where its TX band is received, so a margin at the site for a TX match is not a margin at the receiver (field_location says so).
Free-space propagation (RR No. 21.16).
Angle of arrival is geometric elevation on a spherical Earth, with no refraction.
The given gain applies towards every point. With boresight gain this over-estimates pfd off-axis.
pwr_ds_max is treated as dBW/Hz per a secondary schema note; primary Space Preface confirmation is unavailable.

Power in the reference bandwidth is pwr_ds_max plus 10 log10(reference bandwidth), capped by the row's pep_max, treated as dBW; the emission row used is the one with the most power after that cap. A row without pep_max is not capped.
Maximum gain and power density are used for the whole assignment.

assumptions: Free-space propagation (RR No. 21.16).
Angle of arrival is geometric elevation on a spherical Earth, with no refraction.
The given gain applies towards every point. With boresight gain this over-estimates pfd off-axis.
pwr_ds_max is treated as dBW/Hz per a secondary schema note; primary Space Preface confirmation is unavailable.

Power in the reference bandwidth is pwr_ds_max plus 10 log10(reference bandwidth), capped by the row's pep_max, treated as dBW; the emission row used is the one with the most power after that cap. A row without pep_max is not capped.
Maximum gain and power density are used for the whole assignment.

title: CHINASAT-H-60.5E (CHN) GSO Article 21 limit exceeds under worst-case assumptions; 356 listed stations in band, exceeds at 28

assumptions: 3 of 874 stations have no usable RX or TX frequency and were skipped, so they are not protected here.

RX and TX frequencies are both protected, because Traficom said "every TX is received in Finland" (Discord, 2026-11-07): around a broadcast transmitter, or at the far end of a fixed link. matched_on gives the side each station matched; "both" means its RX and TX bands are the same.
A station's band is its frequency +/- half its channel bandwidth, or half its transmission bandwidth where the channel bandwidth is blank. Where the two differ, the channel bandwidth is used.
The station data is synthetic, per Traficom.

Each station's result comes from the pfd rule's calculation at its coordinates, over the part of the band a limit mask covers. A part with no mask, or a mask that needs an input the filing lacks, counts as no calculation, and a slight edge overlap counts.

Beam coverage is not checked: s_beam gives no boresight in this data, and Traficom said beams "are not relevant" and "the worst case scenario should always be assumed" (Discord, 2026-11-07), so maximum notified gain is applied towards every station.
Antenna direction is not checked: the satellite's is not in the data, and the sheet gives a station direction but few gains, and the receive gain to assume is unanswered (ticket 02 question 14).

Severity follows the strongest evidence at any station: a calculated exceedance is high; a value within 3 dB, an upper bound near or above the limit, or no calculation is medium; a calculated value below, or a satellite below every station's horizon, is low. This severity is the project's choice, not Traficom's.

A station's band is its frequency +/- half its channel bandwidth, or half its transmission bandwidth where the channel bandwidth is blank. Where the two differ, the channel bandwidth is used.
The station data is synthetic, per Traficom.

Each station's result comes from the pfd rule's calculation at its coordinates, over the part of the band a limit mask covers. A part with no mask, or a mask that needs an input the filing lacks, counts as no calculation, and a slight edge overlap counts.

Beam coverage is not checked: s_beam gives no boresight in this data, and Traficom said beams "are not relevant" and "the worst case scenario should always be assumed" (Discord, 2026-11-07), so maximum notified gain is applied towards every station.
Antenna direction is not checked: the satellite's is not in the data, and the sheet gives a station direction but few gains, and the receive gain to assume is unanswered (ticket 02 question 14).

Severity follows the strongest evidence at any station: a calculated exceedance is high; a value within 3 dB, an upper bound near or above the limit, or no calculation is medium; a calculated value below, or a satellite below every station's horizon, is low. This severity is the project's choice, not Traficom's.

title: USASAT-NGSO-8F (USA) transmits on a band of 24 protected station(s): no class 24; pfd exceeds the limit at 24 listed stations under worst-case assumptions

assumptions: Results are possible concerns for expert review; they do not establish compliance.
Records with missing inputs are counted for expert review. Not visible from Finland is a computed result, counted separately.
Mask rows are chosen by band and, for non-GSO, orbit shape, not by the filing's service.

Stations are those in Traficom's list whose RX or TX band overlaps the part of an assignment the mask covers. A GSO value at a station is calculated at its coordinates. A non-GSO value at a station is a sample from the same one-day flight, not a bound; the upper bound has no location, so it applies to the filing and is never given as a station value.
A station's coordinates are not where its TX band is received, so a margin at the site for a TX match is not a margin at the receiver (field_location says so).
The envelope pairs each arrival angle with the shortest distance the orbit can have at that angle, for any node, phase, epoch or argument of perigee, at altitudes from notified perigee to apogee.
Latitude reach comes from inclination and the southernmost Finnish point; relative longitude is unconstrained.
Where orbit_lnk names the orbit rows a beam flies on, only those rows are used. This reading of orbit_lnk is not confirmed against the primary Space Preface.
The envelope is sampled every 0.02 degrees of arrival angle, including every mask breakpoint.
The envelope does not cover station-keeping excursions beyond the notified altitudes, or more than one satellite adding up at a point. It may describe states the satellite never occupies.
Propagation is two-body with no J2, over one day in one-minute steps, for one satellite per distinct orbit shape, so it can miss the worst case and is not an upper bound.

No epoch is notified: at minute 0 the node lies at the notified long_asc (or right_asc if that is absent) as an Earth-fixed longitude, and the satellite is phase_ang past the node. These field meanings are not confirmed against the primary Space Preface.
Free-space propagation (RR No. 21.16).
Angle of arrival is geometric elevation on a spherical Earth, with no refraction.
Maximum notified gain applies towards every point at every moment. With boresight gain this over-estimates pfd off-axis.
pwr_ds_max is treated as dBW/Hz per a secondary schema note; primary Space Preface confirmation is unavailable.

Power in the reference bandwidth is pwr_ds_max plus 10 log10(reference bandwidth), capped by the row's pep_max, treated as dBW; the emission row used is the one with the most power after that cap. A row without pep_max is not capped.

title: KPS-NGSO-A (KOR) NGSO Appendix 5 coordination trigger exceeds in a one-day propagation under worst-case assumptions

assumptions: Results are possible concerns for expert review; they do not establish compliance.
Records with missing inputs are counted for expert review. Not visible from Finland is a computed result, counted separately.
Mask rows are chosen by band and, for non-GSO, orbit shape, not by the filing's service.

Stations are those in Traficom's list whose RX or TX band overlaps the part of an assignment the mask covers. A GSO value at a station is calculated at its coordinates. A non-GSO value at a station is a sample from the same one-day flight, not a bound; the upper bound has no location, so it applies to the filing and is never given as a station value.
A station's coordinates are not where its TX band is received, so a margin at the site for a TX match is not a margin at the receiver (field_location says so).

Maximum gain and power density are used for the whole assignment.

assumptions: Free-space propagation (RR No. 21.16).
Angle of arrival is geometric elevation on a spherical Earth, with no refraction.
The given gain applies towards every point. With boresight gain this over-estimates pfd off-axis.
pwr_ds_max is treated as dBW/Hz per a secondary schema note; primary Space Preface confirmation is unavailable.

Power in the reference bandwidth is pwr_ds_max plus 10 log10(reference bandwidth), capped by the row's pep_max, treated as dBW; the emission row used is the one with the most power after that cap. A row without pep_max is not capped.
Maximum gain and power density are used for the whole assignment.

title: HISPASAT-5-52.5W (E) GSO Article 21 limit exceeds under worst-case assumptions

assumptions: Results are possible concerns for expert review; they do not establish compliance.
Records with missing inputs are counted for expert review. Not visible from Finland is a computed result, counted separately.
Mask rows are chosen by band and, for non-GSO, orbit shape, not by the filing's service.

Stations are those in Traficom's list whose RX or TX band overlaps the part of an assignment the mask covers. A GSO value at a station is calculated at its coordinates. A non-GSO value at a station is a sample from the same one-day flight, not a bound; the upper bound has no location, so it applies to the filing and is never given as a station value.
A station's coordinates are not where its TX band is received, so a margin at the site for a TX match is not a margin at the receiver (field_location says so).
The envelope pairs each arrival angle with the shortest distance the orbit can have at that angle, for any node, phase, epoch or argument of perigee, at altitudes from notified perigee to apogee.
Latitude reach comes from inclination and the southernmost Finnish point; relative longitude is unconstrained.
Where orbit_lnk names the orbit rows a beam flies on, only those rows are used. This reading of orbit_lnk is not confirmed against the primary Space Preface.
The envelope is sampled every 0.02 degrees of arrival angle, including every mask breakpoint.
The envelope does not cover station-keeping excursions beyond the notified altitudes, or more than one satellite adding up at a point. It may describe states the satellite never occupies.
Propagation is two-body with no J2, over one day in one-minute steps, for one satellite per distinct orbit shape, so it can miss the worst case and is not an upper bound.

No epoch is notified: at minute 0 the node lies at the notified long_asc (or right_asc if that is absent) as an Earth-fixed longitude, and the satellite is phase_ang past the node. These field meanings are not confirmed against the primary Space Preface.
Free-space propagation (RR No. 21.16).
Angle of arrival is geometric elevation on a spherical Earth, with no refraction.
Maximum notified gain applies towards every point at every moment. With boresight gain this over-estimates pfd off-axis.
pwr_ds_max is treated as dBW/Hz per a secondary schema note; primary Space Preface confirmation is unavailable.

Power in the reference bandwidth is pwr_ds_max plus 10 log10(reference bandwidth), capped by the row's pep_max, treated as dBW; the emission row used is the one with the most power after that cap. A row without pep_max is not capped.

title: F-SAT-NG-15_B (F) NGSO Article 21 limit exceeds in a one-day propagation under worst-case assumptions; 1008 records not evaluated; 24 listed stations in band, exceeds at 24

assumptions: Results are possible concerns for expert review; they do not establish compliance.
Records with missing inputs are counted for expert review. Not visible from Finland is a computed result, counted separately.
Mask rows are chosen by band and, for non-GSO, orbit shape, not by the filing's service.

Stations are those in Traficom's list whose RX or TX band overlaps the part of an assignment the mask covers. A GSO value at a station is calculated at its coordinates. A non-GSO value at a station is a sample from the same one-day flight, not a bound; the upper bound has no location, so it applies to the filing and is never given as a station value.
A station's coordinates are not where its TX band is received, so a margin at the site for a TX match is not a margin at the receiver (field_location says so).
Free-space propagation (RR No. 21.16).
Angle of arrival is geometric elevation on a spherical Earth, with no refraction.
The given gain applies towards every point. With boresight gain this over-estimates pfd off-axis.
pwr_ds_max is treated as dBW/Hz per a secondary schema note; primary Space Preface confirmation is unavailable.

Power in the reference bandwidth is pwr_ds_max plus 10 log10(reference bandwidth), capped by the row's pep_max, treated as dBW; the emission row used is the one with the most power after that cap. A row without pep_max is not capped.
Maximum gain and power density are used for the whole assignment.

assumptions: Free-space propagation (RR No. 21.16).
Angle of arrival is geometric elevation on a spherical Earth, with no refraction.
The given gain applies towards every point. With boresight gain this over-estimates pfd off-axis.
pwr_ds_max is treated as dBW/Hz per a secondary schema note; primary Space Preface confirmation is unavailable.

Power in the reference bandwidth is pwr_ds_max plus 10 log10(reference bandwidth), capped by the row's pep_max, treated as dBW; the emission row used is the one with the most power after that cap. A row without pep_max is not capped.
Maximum gain and power density are used for the whole assignment.

title: CHINASAT-G-33.5E (CHN) GSO Article 21 limit exceeds under worst-case assumptions; 356 listed stations in band, exceeds at 19

assumptions: Results are possible concerns for expert review; they do not establish compliance.
Records with missing inputs are counted for expert review. Not visible from Finland is a computed result, counted separately.
Mask rows are chosen by band and, for non-GSO, orbit shape, not by the filing's service.

Stations are those in Traficom's list whose RX or TX band overlaps the part of an assignment the mask covers. A GSO value at a station is calculated at its coordinates. A non-GSO value at a station is a sample from the same one-day flight, not a bound; the upper bound has no location, so it applies to the filing and is never given as a station value.
A station's coordinates are not where its TX band is received, so a margin at the site for a TX match is not a margin at the receiver (field_location says so).
The envelope pairs each arrival angle with the shortest distance the orbit can have at that angle, for any node, phase, epoch or argument of perigee, at altitudes from notified perigee to apogee.
Latitude reach comes from inclination and the southernmost Finnish point; relative longitude is unconstrained.
Where orbit_lnk names the orbit rows a beam flies on, only those rows are used. This reading of orbit_lnk is not confirmed against the primary Space Preface.
The envelope is sampled every 0.02 degrees of arrival angle, including every mask breakpoint.
The envelope does not cover station-keeping excursions beyond the notified altitudes, or more than one satellite adding up at a point. It may describe states the satellite never occupies.
Propagation is two-body with no J2, over one day in one-minute steps, for one satellite per distinct orbit shape, so it can miss the worst case and is not an upper bound.

No epoch is notified: at minute 0 the node lies at the notified long_asc (or right_asc if that is absent) as an Earth-fixed longitude, and the satellite is phase_ang past the node. These field meanings are not confirmed against the primary Space Preface.
Free-space propagation (RR No. 21.16).
Angle of arrival is geometric elevation on a spherical Earth, with no refraction.
Maximum notified gain applies towards every point at every moment. With boresight gain this over-estimates pfd off-axis.
pwr_ds_max is treated as dBW/Hz per a secondary schema note; primary Space Preface confirmation is unavailable.

Power in the reference bandwidth is pwr_ds_max plus 10 log10(reference bandwidth), capped by the row's pep_max, treated as dBW; the emission row used is the one with the most power after that cap. A row without pep_max is not capped.

title: USASAT-NGSO-8F (USA) NGSO Article 21 limit exceeds in a one-day propagation under worst-case assumptions; 488 records not evaluated; 24 listed stations in band, exceeds at 24

assumptions: 3 of 874 stations have no usable RX or TX frequency and were skipped, so they are not protected here.

RX and TX frequencies are both protected, because Traficom said "every TX is received in Finland" (Discord, 2026-11-07): around a broadcast transmitter, or at the far end of a fixed link. matched_on gives the side each station matched; "both" means its RX and TX bands are the same.
A station's band is its frequency +/- half its channel bandwidth, or half its transmission bandwidth where the channel bandwidth is blank. Where the two differ, the channel bandwidth is used.
The station data is synthetic, per Traficom.

Each station's result comes from the pfd rule's calculation at its coordinates, over the part of the band a limit mask covers. A part with no mask, or a mask that needs an input the filing lacks, counts as no calculation, and a slight edge overlap counts.

Beam coverage is not checked: s_beam gives no boresight in this data, and Traficom said beams "are not relevant" and "the worst case scenario should always be assumed" (Discord, 2026-11-07), so maximum notified gain is applied towards every station.
Antenna direction is not checked: the satellite's is not in the data, and the sheet gives a station direction but few gains, and the receive gain to assume is unanswered (ticket 02 question 14).

Severity follows the strongest evidence at any station: a calculated exceedance is high; a value within 3 dB, an upper bound near or above the limit, or no calculation is medium; a calculated value below, or a satellite below every station's horizon, is low. This severity is the project's choice, not Traficom's.

assumptions: Results are possible concerns for expert review; they do not establish compliance.
Records with missing inputs are counted for expert review. Not visible from Finland is a computed result, counted separately.
Mask rows are chosen by band and, for non-GSO, orbit shape, not by the filing's service.

Stations are those in Traficom's list whose RX or TX band overlaps the part of an assignment the mask covers. A GSO value at a station is calculated at its coordinates. A non-GSO value at a station is a sample from the same one-day flight, not a bound; the upper bound has no location, so it applies to the filing and is never given as a station value.
A station's coordinates are not where its TX band is received, so a margin at the site for a TX match is not a margin at the receiver (field_location says so).
The envelope pairs each arrival angle with the shortest distance the orbit can have at that angle, for any node, phase, epoch or argument of perigee, at altitudes from notified perigee to apogee.
Latitude reach comes from inclination and the southernmost Finnish point; relative longitude is unconstrained.

The envelope is sampled every 0.02 degrees of arrival angle, including every mask breakpoint.
The envelope does not cover station-keeping excursions beyond the notified altitudes, or more than one satellite adding up at a point. It may describe states the satellite never occupies.
Propagation is two-body with no J2, over one day in one-minute steps, for one satellite per distinct orbit shape, so it can miss the worst case and is not an upper bound.

No epoch is notified: at minute 0 the node lies at the notified long_asc (or right_asc if that is absent) as an Earth-fixed longitude, and the satellite is phase_ang past the node. These field meanings are not confirmed against the primary Space Preface.
Free-space propagation (RR No. 21.16).
Angle of arrival is geometric elevation on a spherical Earth, with no refraction.
Maximum notified gain applies towards every point at every moment. With boresight gain this over-estimates pfd off-axis.
pwr_ds_max is treated as dBW/Hz per a secondary schema note; primary Space Preface confirmation is unavailable.

Power in the reference bandwidth is pwr_ds_max plus 10 log10(reference bandwidth), capped by the row's pep_max, treated as dBW; the emission row used is the one with the most power after that cap. A row without pep_max is not capped.

title: USASAT-NGSO-8E (USA) NGSO Article 21 limit exceeds in a one-day propagation under worst-case assumptions; 488 records not evaluated; 24 listed stations in band, exceeds at 24

assumptions: 3 of 874 stations have no usable RX or TX frequency and were skipped, so they are not protected here.

RX and TX frequencies are both protected, because Traficom said "every TX is received in Finland" (Discord, 2026-11-07): around a broadcast transmitter, or at the far end of a fixed link. matched_on gives the side each station matched; "both" means its RX and TX bands are the same.
A station's band is its frequency +/- half its channel bandwidth, or half its transmission bandwidth where the channel bandwidth is blank. Where the two differ, the channel bandwidth is used.
The station data is synthetic, per Traficom.

Each station's result comes from the pfd rule's calculation at its coordinates, over the part of the band a limit mask covers. A part with no mask, or a mask that needs an input the filing lacks, counts as no calculation, and a slight edge overlap counts.

Beam coverage is not checked: s_beam gives no boresight in this data, and Traficom said beams "are not relevant" and "the worst case scenario should always be assumed" (Discord, 2026-11-07), so maximum notified gain is applied towards every station.
Antenna direction is not checked: the satellite's is not in the data, and the sheet gives a station direction but few gains, and the receive gain to assume is unanswered (ticket 02 question 14).

Severity follows the strongest evidence at any station: a calculated exceedance is high; a value within 3 dB, an upper bound near or above the limit, or no calculation is medium; a calculated value below, or a satellite below every station's horizon, is low. This severity is the project's choice, not Traficom's.

title: MULA (PHL) NGSO Article 21 limit: upper bound above the limit; no time-sampled result; 66 listed stations in band

assumptions: 3 of 874 stations have no usable RX or TX frequency and were skipped, so they are not protected here.

RX and TX frequencies are both protected, because Traficom said "every TX is received in Finland" (Discord, 2026-11-07): around a broadcast transmitter, or at the far end of a fixed link. matched_on gives the side each station matched; "both" means its RX and TX bands are the same.
A station's band is its frequency +/- half its channel bandwidth, or half its transmission bandwidth where the channel bandwidth is blank. Where the two differ, the channel bandwidth is used.
The station data is synthetic, per Traficom.

Each station's result comes from the pfd rule's calculation at its coordinates, over the part of the band a limit mask covers. A part with no mask, or a mask that needs an input the filing lacks, counts as no calculation, and a slight edge overlap counts.

Beam coverage is not checked: s_beam gives no boresight in this data, and Traficom said beams "are not relevant" and "the worst case scenario should always be assumed" (Discord, 2026-11-07), so maximum notified gain is applied towards every station.
Antenna direction is not checked: the satellite's is not in the data, and the sheet gives a station direction but few gains, and the receive gain to assume is unanswered (ticket 02 question 14).

Severity follows the strongest evidence at any station: a calculated exceedance is high; a value within 3 dB, an upper bound near or above the limit, or no calculation is medium; a calculated value below, or a satellite below every station's horizon, is low. This severity is the project's choice, not Traficom's.

title: USASAT-30-3 (USA) transmits on a band of 18 protected station(s): Earth station (RX) 1, MUUT 1, MVV 4, no class 12; pfd within 3 dB below the limit at a listed station

assumptions: Results are possible concerns for expert review; they do not establish compliance.
Records with missing inputs are counted for expert review. Not visible from Finland is a computed result, counted separately.
Mask rows are chosen by band and, for non-GSO, orbit shape, not by the filing's service.

Stations are those in Traficom's list whose RX or TX band overlaps the part of an assignment the mask covers. A GSO value at a station is calculated at its coordinates. A non-GSO value at a station is a sample from the same one-day flight, not a bound; the upper bound has no location, so it applies to the filing and is never given as a station value.
A station's coordinates are not where its TX band is received, so a margin at the site for a TX match is not a margin at the receiver (field_location says so).
The envelope pairs each arrival angle with the shortest distance the orbit can have at that angle, for any node, phase, epoch or argument of perigee, at altitudes from notified perigee to apogee.
Latitude reach comes from inclination and the southernmost Finnish point; relative longitude is unconstrained.
Where orbit_lnk names the orbit rows a beam flies on, only those rows are used. This reading of orbit_lnk is not confirmed against the primary Space Preface.
The envelope is sampled every 0.02 degrees of arrival angle, including every mask breakpoint.
The envelope does not cover station-keeping excursions beyond the notified altitudes, or more than one satellite adding up at a point. It may describe states the satellite never occupies.
Propagation is two-body with no J2, over one day in one-minute steps, for one satellite per distinct orbit shape, so it can miss the worst case and is not an upper bound.

No epoch is notified: at minute 0 the node lies at the notified long_asc (or right_asc if that is absent) as an Earth-fixed longitude, and the satellite is phase_ang past the node. These field meanings are not confirmed against the primary Space Preface.
Free-space propagation (RR No. 21.16).
Angle of arrival is geometric elevation on a spherical Earth, with no refraction.
Maximum notified gain applies towards every point at every moment. With boresight gain this over-estimates pfd off-axis.
pwr_ds_max is treated as dBW/Hz per a secondary schema note; primary Space Preface confirmation is unavailable.

Power in the reference bandwidth is pwr_ds_max plus 10 log10(reference bandwidth), capped by the row's pep_max, treated as dBW; the emission row used is the one with the most power after that cap. A row without pep_max is not capped.

title: NSL-1 (ISR) NGSO Article 21 limit: upper bound within 3 dB below the limit; not a compliance finding; 9 records not evaluated; 14 listed stations in band

assumptions: 3 of 874 stations have no usable RX or TX frequency and were skipped, so they are not protected here.

RX and TX frequencies are both protected, because Traficom said "every TX is received in Finland" (Discord, 2026-11-07): around a broadcast transmitter, or at the far end of a fixed link. matched_on gives the side each station matched; "both" means its RX and TX bands are the same.
A station's band is its frequency +/- half its channel bandwidth, or half its transmission bandwidth where the channel bandwidth is blank. Where the two differ, the channel bandwidth is used.
The station data is synthetic, per Traficom.

Each station's result comes from the pfd rule's calculation at its coordinates, over the part of the band a limit mask covers. A part with no mask, or a mask that needs an input the filing lacks, counts as no calculation, and a slight edge overlap counts.

Beam coverage is not checked: s_beam gives no boresight in this data, and Traficom said beams "are not relevant" and "the worst case scenario should always be assumed" (Discord, 2026-11-07), so maximum notified gain is applied towards every station.
Antenna direction is not checked: the satellite's is not in the data, and the sheet gives a station direction but few gains, and the receive gain to assume is unanswered (ticket 02 question 14).

Severity follows the strongest evidence at any station: a calculated exceedance is high; a value within 3 dB, an upper bound near or above the limit, or no calculation is medium; a calculated value below, or a satellite below every station's horizon, is low. This severity is the project's choice, not Traficom's.

Mask rows are chosen by band and, for non-GSO, orbit shape, not by the filing's service.

Stations are those in Traficom's list whose RX or TX band overlaps the part of an assignment the mask covers. A GSO value at a station is calculated at its coordinates. Propagation is two-body with no J2, over one day in one-minute steps, for one satellite per distinct orbit shape, so it can miss the worst case and is not an upper bound.

title: GARAI-B (S) NGSO Article 21 limit: upper bound within 3 dB below the limit; not a compliance finding; 88 listed stations in band

assumptions: 3 of 874 stations have no usable RX or TX frequency and were skipped, so they are not protected here.

RX and TX frequencies are both protected, because Traficom said "every TX is received in Finland" (Discord, 2026-11-07): around a broadcast transmitter, or at the far end of a fixed link. matched_on gives the side each station matched; "both" means its RX and TX bands are the same.
A station's band is its frequency +/- half its channel bandwidth, or half its transmission bandwidth where the channel bandwidth is blank. Where the two differ, the channel bandwidth is used.
The station data is synthetic, per Traficom.

Each station's result comes from the pfd rule's calculation at its coordinates, over the part of the band a limit mask covers. A part with no mask, or a mask that needs an input the filing lacks, counts as no calculation, and a slight edge overlap counts.

Beam coverage is not checked: s_beam gives no boresight in this data, and Traficom said beams "are not relevant" and "the worst case scenario should always be assumed" (Discord, 2026-11-07), so maximum notified gain is applied towards every station.
Antenna direction is not checked: the satellite's is not in the data, and the sheet gives a station direction but few gains, and the receive gain to assume is unanswered (ticket 02 question 14).

Severity follows the strongest evidence at any station: a calculated exceedance is high; a value within 3 dB, an upper bound near or above the limit, or no calculation is medium; a calculated value below, or a satellite below every station's horizon, is low. This severity is the project's choice, not Traficom's.

title: QATARGOV-G1-25.5E (QAT) transmits on a band of 46 protected station(s): no class 46; no pfd calculation covers some of these stations

assumptions: 3 of 874 stations have no usable RX or TX frequency and were skipped, so they are not protected here.

RX and TX frequencies are both protected, because Traficom said "every TX is received in Finland" (Discord, 2026-11-07): around a broadcast transmitter, or at the far end of a fixed link. matched_on gives the side each station matched; "both" means its RX and TX bands are the same.
A station's band is its frequency +/- half its channel bandwidth, or half its transmission bandwidth where the channel bandwidth is blank. Where the two differ, the channel bandwidth is used.
The station data is synthetic, per Traficom.

Each station's result comes from the pfd rule's calculation at its coordinates, over the part of the band a limit mask covers. A part with no mask, or a mask that needs an input the filing lacks, counts as no calculation, and a slight edge overlap counts.

Beam coverage is not checked: s_beam gives no boresight in this data, and Traficom said beams "are not relevant" and "the worst case scenario should always be assumed" (Discord, 2026-11-07), so maximum notified gain is applied towards every station.
Antenna direction is not checked: the satellite's is not in the data, and the sheet gives a station direction but few gains, and the receive gain to assume is unanswered (ticket 02 question 14).

Severity follows the strongest evidence at any station: a calculated exceedance is high; a value within 3 dB, an upper bound near or above the limit, or no calculation is medium; a calculated value below, or a satellite below every station's horizon, is low. This severity is the project's choice, not Traficom's.

title: SOLAR SENTRY (D) transmits on a band of 32 protected station(s): FX 32; only the filing's upper bound is near or above the limit

assumptions: Results are possible concerns for expert review; they do not establish compliance.
Records with missing inputs are counted for expert review. Not visible from Finland is a computed result, counted separately.
Mask rows are chosen by band and, for non-GSO, orbit shape, not by the filing's service.

Stations are those in Traficom's list whose RX or TX band overlaps the part of an assignment the mask covers. A GSO value at a station is calculated at its coordinates. A non-GSO value at a station is a sample from the same one-day flight, not a bound; the upper bound has no location, so it applies to the filing and is never given as a station value.
A station's coordinates are not where its TX band is received, so a margin at the site for a TX match is not a margin at the receiver (field_location says so).
The envelope pairs each arrival angle with the shortest distance the orbit can have at that angle, for any node, phase, epoch or argument of perigee, at altitudes from notified perigee to apogee.
Latitude reach comes from inclination and the southernmost Finnish point; relative longitude is unconstrained.
Where orbit_lnk names the orbit rows a beam flies on, only those rows are used. This reading of orbit_lnk is not confirmed against the primary Space Preface.
The envelope is sampled every 0.02 degrees of arrival angle, including every mask breakpoint.
The envelope does not cover station-keeping excursions beyond the notified altitudes, or more than one satellite adding up at a point. It may describe states the satellite never occupies.
Propagation is two-body with no J2, over one day in one-minute steps, for one satellite per distinct orbit shape, so it can miss the worst case and is not an upper bound.

No epoch is notified: at minute 0 the node lies at the notified long_asc (or right_asc if that is absent) as an Earth-fixed longitude, and the satellite is phase_ang past the node. These field meanings are not confirmed against the primary Space Preface.
Free-space propagation (RR No. 21.16).
Angle of arrival is geometric elevation on a spherical Earth, with no refraction.
Maximum notified gain applies towards every point at every moment. With boresight gain this over-estimates pfd off-axis.
pwr_ds_max is treated as dBW/Hz per a secondary schema note; primary Space Preface confirmation is unavailable.

Power in the reference bandwidth is pwr_ds_max plus 10 log10(reference bandwidth), capped by the row's pep_max, treated as dBW; the emission row used is the one with the most power after that cap. A row without pep_max is not capped.

Free-space propagation (RR No. 21.16).

title: LUNAR-R5 (CHN) NGSO Article 21 limit not evaluated; missing earth_orbit; 324 listed stations in band

assumptions: Results are possible concerns for expert review; they do not establish compliance.
Records with missing inputs are counted for expert review. Not visible from Finland is a computed result, counted separately.
Mask rows are chosen by band and, for non-GSO, orbit shape, not by the filing's service.
The envelope pairs each arrival angle with the shortest distance the orbit can have at that angle, for any node, phase, epoch or argument of perigee, at altitudes from notified perigee to apogee.
Latitude reach comes from inclination and the southernmost Finnish point; relative longitude is unconstrained.
Where orbit_lnk names the orbit rows a beam flies on, only those rows are used. This reading of orbit_lnk is not confirmed against the primary Space Preface.
The envelope is sampled every 0.02 degrees of arrival angle, including every mask breakpoint.
The envelope does not cover station-keeping excursions beyond the notified altitudes, or more than one satellite adding up at a point. It may describe states the satellite never occupies.
Propagation is two-body with no J2, over one day in one-minute steps, for one satellite per distinct orbit shape, so it can miss the worst case and is not an upper bound.

No epoch is notified: at minute 0 the node lies at the notified long_asc (or right_asc if that is absent) as an Earth-fixed longitude, and the satellite is phase_ang past the node. These field meanings are not confirmed against the primary Space Preface.
Free-space propagation (RR No. 21.16).
Angle of arrival is geometric elevation on a spherical Earth, with no refraction.
Maximum notified gain applies towards every point at every moment. With boresight gain this over-estimates pfd off-axis.
pwr_ds_max is treated as dBW/Hz per a secondary schema note; primary Space Preface confirmation is unavailable.

Power in the reference bandwidth is pwr_ds_max plus 10 log10(reference bandwidth), capped by the row's pep_max, treated as dBW; the emission row used is the one with the most power after that cap. A row without pep_max is not capped.

title: TYSAR-01 (CHN) transmits on a band of 14 protected station(s): Earth station (RX) 1, MUUT 13; no pfd calculation covers some of these stations

assumptions: 3 of 874 stations have no usable RX or TX frequency and were skipped, so they are not protected here.

RX and TX frequencies are both protected, because Traficom said "every TX is received in Finland" (Discord, 2026-11-07): around a broadcast transmitter, or at the far end of a fixed link. matched_on gives the side each station matched; "both" means its RX and TX bands are the same.
A station's band is its frequency +/- half its channel bandwidth, or half its transmission bandwidth where the channel bandwidth is blank. Where the two differ, the channel bandwidth is used.
The station data is synthetic, per Traficom.

Each station's result comes from the pfd rule's calculation at its coordinates, over the part of the band a limit mask covers. A part with no mask, or a mask that needs an input the filing lacks, counts as no calculation, and a slight edge overlap counts.

Beam coverage is not checked: s_beam gives no boresight in this data, and Traficom said beams "are not relevant" and "the worst case scenario should always be assumed" (Discord, 2026-11-07), so maximum notified gain is applied towards every station.
Antenna direction is not checked: the satellite's is not in the data, and the sheet gives a station direction but few gains, and the receive gain to assume is unanswered (ticket 02 question 14).

Severity follows the strongest evidence at any station: a calculated exceedance is high; a value within 3 dB, an upper bound near or above the limit, or no calculation is medium; a calculated value below, or a satellite below every station's horizon, is low. This severity is the project's choice, not Traficom's.

title: MTG-EUM_9.5E (D) transmits on a band of 56 protected station(s): FX 54, MVV 2; no pfd calculation covers some of these stations

assumptions: Results are possible concerns for expert review; they do not establish compliance.
Records with missing inputs are counted for expert review. Not visible from Finland is a computed result, counted separately.
Mask rows are chosen by band and, for non-GSO, orbit shape, not by the filing's service.

Stations are those in Traficom's list whose RX or TX band overlaps the part of an assignment the mask covers. A GSO value at a station is calculated at its coordinates. A non-GSO value at a station is a sample from the same one-day flight, not a bound; the upper bound has no location, so it applies to the filing and is never given as a station value.
A station's coordinates are not where its TX band is received, so a margin at the site for a TX match is not a margin at the receiver (field_location says so).
The envelope pairs each arrival angle with the shortest distance the orbit can have at that angle, for any node, phase, epoch or argument of perigee, at altitudes from notified perigee to apogee.
Latitude reach comes from inclination and the southernmost Finnish point; relative longitude is unconstrained.
Where orbit_lnk names the orbit rows a beam flies on, only those rows are used. This reading of orbit_lnk is not confirmed against the primary Space Preface.
The envelope is sampled every 0.02 degrees of arrival angle, including every mask breakpoint.
The envelope does not cover station-keeping excursions beyond the notified altitudes, or more than one satellite adding up at a point. It may describe states the satellite never occupies.
Propagation is two-body with no J2, over one day in one-minute steps, for one satellite per distinct orbit shape, so it can miss the worst case and is not an upper bound.

No epoch is notified: at minute 0 the node lies at the notified long_asc (or right_asc if that is absent) as an Earth-fixed longitude, and the satellite is phase_ang past the node. These field meanings are not confirmed against the primary Space Preface.
Free-space propagation (RR No. 21.16).
Angle of arrival is geometric elevation on a spherical Earth, with no refraction.
Maximum notified gain applies towards every point at every moment. With boresight gain this over-estimates pfd off-axis.
pwr_ds_max is treated as dBW/Hz per a secondary schema note; primary Space Preface confirmation is unavailable.

Power in the reference bandwidth is pwr_ds_max plus 10 log10(reference bandwidth), capped by the row's pep_max, treated as dBW; the emission row used is the one with the most power after that cap. A row without pep_max is not capped.

title: GD-B (CHN) NGSO Article 21 limit: upper bound below the limit for this orbit and these inputs; not a compliance finding; expert review required; 2 listed stations in band

assumptions: 3 of 874 stations have no usable RX or TX frequency and were skipped, so they are not protected here.

RX and TX frequencies are both protected, because Traficom said "every TX is received in Finland" (Discord, 2026-11-07): around a broadcast transmitter, or at the far end of a fixed link. matched_on gives the side each station matched; "both" means its RX and TX bands are the same.
A station's band is its frequency +/- half its channel bandwidth, or half its transmission bandwidth where the channel bandwidth is blank. Where the two differ, the channel bandwidth is used.
The station data is synthetic, per Traficom.

Each station's result comes from the pfd rule's calculation at its coordinates, over the part of the band a limit mask covers. A part with no mask, or a mask that needs an input the filing lacks, counts as no calculation, and a slight edge overlap counts.

Beam coverage is not checked: s_beam gives no boresight in this data, and Traficom said beams "are not relevant" and "the worst case scenario should always be assumed" (Discord, 2026-11-07), so maximum notified gain is applied towards every station.
Antenna direction is not checked: the satellite's is not in the data, and the sheet gives a station direction but few gains, and the receive gain to assume is unanswered (ticket 02 question 14).

Severity follows the strongest evidence at any station: a calculated exceedance is high; a value within 3 dB, an upper bound near or above the limit, or no calculation is medium; a calculated value below, or a satellite below every station's horizon, is low. This severity is the project's choice, not Traficom's.

title: GY-2 (CHN) NGSO Article 21 limit: upper bound below the limit for this orbit and these inputs; not a compliance finding; expert review required; 2 listed stations in band

assumptions: 3 of 874 stations have no usable RX or TX frequency and were skipped, so they are not protected here.

RX and TX frequencies are both protected, because Traficom said "every TX is received in Finland" (Discord, 2026-11-07): around a broadcast transmitter, or at the far end of a fixed link. matched_on gives the side each station matched; "both" means its RX and TX bands are the same.
A station's band is its frequency +/- half its channel bandwidth, or half its transmission bandwidth where the channel bandwidth is blank. Where the two differ, the channel bandwidth is used.
The station data is synthetic, per Traficom.

Each station's result comes from the pfd rule's calculation at its coordinates, over the part of the band a limit mask covers. A part with no mask, or a mask that needs an input the filing lacks, counts as no calculation, and a slight edge overlap counts.

Beam coverage is not checked: s_beam gives no boresight in this data, and Traficom said beams "are not relevant" and "the worst case scenario should always be assumed" (Discord, 2026-11-07), so maximum notified gain is applied towards every station.
Antenna direction is not checked: the satellite's is not in the data, and the sheet gives a station direction but few gains, and the receive gain to assume is unanswered (ticket 02 question 14).

Severity follows the strongest evidence at any station: a calculated exceedance is high; a value within 3 dB, an upper bound near or above the limit, or no calculation is medium; a calculated value below, or a satellite below every station's horizon, is low. This severity is the project's choice, not Traficom's.

title: JZ-3 (CHN) NGSO Article 21 limit: upper bound below the limit for this orbit and these inputs; not a compliance finding; expert review required; 2 listed stations in band

assumptions: 3 of 874 stations have no usable RX or TX frequency and were skipped, so they are not protected here.

RX and TX frequencies are both protected, because Traficom said "every TX is received in Finland" (Discord, 2026-11-07): around a broadcast transmitter, or at the far end of a fixed link. matched_on gives the side each station matched; "both" means its RX and TX bands are the same.
A station's band is its frequency +/- half its channel bandwidth, or half its transmission bandwidth where the channel bandwidth is blank. Where the two differ, the channel bandwidth is used.
The station data is synthetic, per Traficom.

Each station's result comes from the pfd rule's calculation at its coordinates, over the part of the band a limit mask covers. A part with no mask, or a mask that needs an input the filing lacks, counts as no calculation, and a slight edge overlap counts.

Beam coverage is not checked: s_beam gives no boresight in this data, and Traficom said beams "are not relevant" and "the worst case scenario should always be assumed" (Discord, 2026-11-07), so maximum notified gain is applied towards every station.
Antenna direction is not checked: the satellite's is not in the data, and the sheet gives a station direction but few gains, and the receive gain to assume is unanswered (ticket 02 question 14).

Severity follows the strongest evidence at any station: a calculated exceedance is high; a value within 3 dB, an upper bound near or above the limit, or no calculation is medium; a calculated value below, or a satellite below every station's horizon, is low. This severity is the project's choice, not Traficom's.

assumptions: Results are possible concerns for expert review; they do not establish compliance.
Records with missing inputs are counted for expert review. Not visible from Finland is a computed result, counted separately.
Mask rows are chosen by band and, for non-GSO, orbit shape, not by the filing's service.

Stations are those in Traficom's list whose RX or TX band overlaps the part of an assignment the mask covers. A GSO value at a station is calculated at its coordinates. A non-GSO value at a station is a sample from the same one-day flight, not a bound; the upper bound has no location, so it applies to the filing and is never given as a station value.
A station's coordinates are not where its TX band is received, so a margin at the site for a TX match is not a margin at the receiver (field_location says so).
Free-space propagation (RR No. 21.16).
Angle of arrival is geometric elevation on a spherical Earth, with no refraction.
The given gain applies towards every point. With boresight gain this over-estimates pfd off-axis.

Power in the reference bandwidth is pwr_ds_max plus 10 log10(reference bandwidth), capped by the row's pep_max, treated as dBW; the emission row used is the one with the most power after that cap. A row without pep_max is not capped.
Maximum gain and power density are used for the whole assignment.
